properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/06/2023 to ARMAC RESOURCES LLC in Warren City, Warren county. 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/05/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8157634
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 9/06/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator had a rig attempt to drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run would have taken place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. The rig failed to drill down to 550' and it was decided to cement the remaining tubing into the well. Top of cement is now at 288.23' with approx. 102' of tubing encapsulated within the well bore. ARMAC has now contracted Hornburg drilling to attempt to drill and clean out the well-bore to a depth of 550'. At the time of inspection Hornburg Drilling Rig 78 has drilled with a 4-1/2" work string and a 6-1/8" bit from 288' to 350' and were putting new buttons on their drill bit. Returns have been cement till and chunks of steel. Drilling will resume tomorrow.

OGI Matt Woods requested that a WQS follow up because of potential surface pollution concerns regarding a plastic-lined pit observed during IR 4269845.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- No equipment related to production and/or well plugging operations was observed on site. The plastic-lined pit documented in IR 4269845 was not observed during this inspection (Photos 11 and 19). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site at the time of inspection. No plugging monument was observed at the former location of the well. The API number and Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) were found on site (Photos 16 and 17).- The access road and well site remain heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. Some mulch and seed was observed on site. However, the mulch and seed implemented on site is inadequate, as large portions of exposed soil are observable (Photos 12-15 and 20-21).- No perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site. No E and S Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.Based on today's inspection, the violations issued in IR 4263564 against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site will remain outstanding. An additional violation is being issued in this inspection for failure to implement adequate seed and temporary stabilization on areas that were disturbed by well plugging operations.The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The Department requests that the Operator provide an electronic copy of the Control and Disposal Plan and provide clarification regarding the purpose of the plastic-lined pit observed during the time of IR 4269845, what it contained, and method of disposal used. Please provide this clarification no later than 9/29/2026. Additional violations may be forthcoming upon receipt and review of the clarification from the Operator.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 6/09/2021
Comments: Prior to inspection: On 6/2/21 Range Resource's Derek Zofchak reported a produced water spill estimated at 15 gallons resulting from a pump operator "overfilling a tub" during site activities. The spill did not reportedly impact or threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth but extended roughly 60' off the site and down a fill slope. On 6/9/21 an incident inspection of the Indian Point Unit 1 Well Pad was conducted in response to an operator reported spill (CTS ID: 357202). The following was observed: >>Communication with the operator in conjunction with the inspection indicated that the spill had been fully remediated and a roll off box of impacted material was taken for disposal. >>Work crews were on site at the time of inspection adding compost filter sock (CFS) and conducting site maintenance. (Photo #1) >>An erosion channel was noted leading to the well pad near the juncture of the site access road and the pad. Remediation and stabilization are recommended. (Photo #2) >>The site was reportedly being prepared for upgrades with numerous liners, tanks and other equipment, and earth work noted. The site is less than five acres and does not appear to ever have/need an ESCGP. (Photo #3) >>Background conductivity readings as measured in several areas less than ten feet off pad were between 0.15-0.20mS. (Photo #4) >>In general conductivity readings around the pad area where between 0.4-0.8mS which may be related to pad materials (limestone) or residual impact. (Photo #5) >>The remediated spill area appeared to be as described by the operator with conductivity readings at background levels. (Photo #6) >>An area of saturated soil roughly 10'x5' near the pad liner/containment and directly adjacent to the remediated primary spill area was also significantly impacted with conductivity readings of 8.5-9.2mS. This may indicate additional spilled production fluids having leaked under the pad liner and panels. Follow up inspection needed once liner and pads are moved. The findings, a request for notification when the expanded spill area is accessible, and the need for follow up inspections were immediately communicated to Range Resources' Dennis Furmanek and Derek Zofchak. (Photo #7-8) >>Determination: The initially reported spill and the identified area of residual impact constitute violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.57(a), and 35 P.S. § 6018.301 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-06-03 to Catalyst Energy Inc in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Catalyst Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-03
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 886010
Permit API: 083-55763
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-03
Comments: This well is a producing combination well with an electric powered motor attached. The well was being operated at the time of this inspection. The stuffing box gasket failed, and at the time of visit, the well was pumping oil and brine out to the ground. The fluid plus runoff from recent rains allowed the oil to flow down the road approximately 150 feet, entering a puddle near a culvert that carried an UNT Chappel Fork. The operator was contacted to get cleanup efforts underway. The well was shut off and pads were placed down to collect as much oil from the track as possible. No oil was apparent in the UNT. Rain stopped and there was a decrease in the flow of oil down the track. The pumper for this lease showed up and was able to leave and get a vacuum truck to come collect the water/oil in the puddle. Marking tape was placed so that public vehicles would not drive through the oil. It is estimated that 15-20 gallons of fluid, including 3-5 gallons of oil were released from the well due to the stuffing box failure. Most pooled in a low spot next to the wellhead. Some ran down the access road, again pooling in a puddle of water that was previously mentioned. The brine mostly stayed in place in the soil or vegetation. A puddle within 10 feet of the wellhead showed over 20 mS/cm conductivity, while checking further toward the extent of the spill showed much lower numbers. The final puddle registered under 0.1 mS/cm. The operator had the vac truck on the way and after later discussions, it was decided that they would need to excavate the area around the wellhead to remove impacted soil. Further follow up will be done on this site as possible.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in the afternoon with cold, cloudy weather conditions and 34 degrees. Last inspection performed on 3/22/2018, more than 5 years ago. Wellhead is located in a soybean, Agriculture field ~250' East and in fairly close, visible proximity to surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, lower left side production tubular valve cracked open to ports and drip/domestic house gas meter run with port valves closed, in line standpipe tank with pressure gauge reading ~900 psi, open valve to drip and open supply valve after meter, lower production tubular right side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on right side of head (opposite meter) to sales/surface equipment has closed valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #2 and #3). Meter reading (photo #4). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. Due to close, visible proximity of wellhead to surface facility a well label/marker is not necessary, but the Department recommends affixing a well label/marker to wellhead. Some fair corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by an earthen dike (photo #5). Valve open on main tubular feeding facility/separator with open valves to and from separator (photo #6). A 7-day production chart is present with no date and no real distinct markings only wrapping, circular ink rings (photo #7). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank is blank with no information about the well. The well posting needs replaced to include all well details and Operator contact information address and phone number (photo #8). Trace to occasionally fair corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Operator submitted 2022 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well stating 365 psig. The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2022 is blank and indicates that this well was not in production during the 2022 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having blank production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the '22, '21, '20, '19, '18, '17, '16, and '15 annual production reports. The last reported production was in 2014 with 72 Mcf recorded over 365 days. During todays inspection, OGI spoke to the land/home owner who stated that house gas is being provided currently and has been provided steadily over the years. Given this information and todays inspection, the well is not abandoned and has been providing house gas to the land/home owner. This is an active, producing well providing house gas to the land/home owner.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/24/2022
Comments: This well was inspected as part of a routine inspection. The well is currently awaiting a service rig, per the operator, and has not been recently pumped. It appears as though a leak occurred on this site sometime in the past year, and it was covered with absorbent peat and then left. The spill was not reported to DEP. The quantity of oil spilled is unknown, but appears to be greater than 5 gallons and less than one barrel. Oil stained soil with absorbent peat is noted in an L shape approximately 10 feet wide and 30 feet long that extends to the edge of the location. Absorbent peat is noted closer to the edge of the site, primarily. A small UNT of Briggs Run begins at the edge of the site. One oil soaked pad was noted in this ditch lone, although no oil was noted in the ditch at this time. The operator was contacted and they arrived on site to begin assessment and cleanup on 8/25. Per the operator, the spill occurred over this past winter and the well pumper covered the spill with peat sorb, which then settled as it was not cleaned up as the winter went on. Spring melt allowed the material to run to the edge of the site. Per the operator, the employee is no longer with the company. Cleanup should be completed in the next few days. Followup inspection will be performed at that time.The operator was also asked about the steep and rutted access roads on this lease and said that they have recently acquired a new bulldozer and intend to grade and fix lease roads soon.

Violation ID: 8185716
Permit API: 003-22651
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/30/2024
Comments: On April 30, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resource's Drape James Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued: 3/29/23 and expires: 3/28/28) located in Frazer Township, Allegheny County in response to CTS #380249.Nick Reda of Range Resources reportedly noticed on April 30, 2024 at 8:15AM an approximately 84 gallon release of water based drill mud on the graveled well pad in several areas. Nick notified the emergency hotline by 10:02AM and believes there is likely one or more holes in the secondary containment causing fluid to leech out from under the containment.The findings of this inspection are as follows: Upon walking the well pad, orange spray paint markings were made by Nick to designate the affected areas plus some buffer space since it was starting to rain. 7 distinct designated areas were observed, some areas had puddles of fluid in them while other areas had stained gravel. Some puddles were cloudy while others appeared to have a sheen to them. Pooling of fluid with sheen were also seen on the secondary containment in some areas.Conductivity readings were taken inside the different spill areas as well as adjacent to the marked spill areas to determine whether any areas outside of these markings were contaminated as well. A background conductivity reading was taken at the well pad perimeter upslope (0.0159 mS) and the rest of the readings are as follows: inside Spill Area 1: 12.6 mS, outside of Spill Area 1: 0.085 mS, inside of Spill Area 3: 1.529 mS, inside of Spill Area 4: 2.05 mS, outside of Spill Area 4: 0.011 mS, from in a cloudy puddle seen in Spill Area 5: Over Range, outside of Spill Area 5: 0.011 mS, inside Spill Area 6: 1.762 mS, from a sheen puddle seen in Spill Area 7: Over range, and lastly 3 readings were taken in stained sediment around the well pad to see if there were other contaminated areas: 0.042 mS, 0.693 mS and 0.0227 mS. These readings subjugate that a release has in fact occurred, that the areas marked by Nick are the contaminated areas, and that at the time of the inspection the release had not appeared to seep past the visibly marked contaminated areas. The perimeter of the well site on the side of the pad where the release occurred was walked and 2 key way drains were investigated. Both drains were dry and soil conductivity readings were taken at each one (0.091 mS and 0.027 mS). Based on these conductivity readings and the lack of fluid coming from the drains, it does not appear that at this time, the release has seeped down into the drainage system.While onsite, SPSI arrived to begin the remediation process. A skid steer was observed scraping up contaminated gravel into piles, a vacuum truck and 2 clamshell roll off dumpsters were scheduled to arrive today and once they do, the truck will suck up all contaminated fluids and the skid steer will pick up all reachable contaminated gravel/sediment and place it in the dumpsters for disposal. Nick stated that Range was not sure on an exact area in which the release originated from. In theory, Range believes there to be one or more holes/tears in the secondary containment, but none of them have reportedly been discovered at the time of the inspection. Nick stated that the drill rig has two more weeks on site. During these two weeks as equipment is removed and once the drill rig is gone, Range plans to continue inspecting the secondary containment, specifically in areas that currently have equipment on top of it. Any further releases will continue to be cleaned and any holes/tears will be repaired as they are found. The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release and promptly find and repair any holes or tears in the secondary containment to prevent any further releases. The Department also requests the Operator notify the Department of any further releases or impacts that occur and supply the Department with secondary containment inspection reports within 2 business days of receipt of this report.

Comments: On 2/24/26 at 9:11 AM, I arrived at the Walker 1616 OG Well to conduct a Routine/Complete Inspection. At the time of the inspection all the valves on the well tree were shut (Photograph #4). The well appears to not be producing based on the valve alignment and absence of chart in the meter box. (Photograph #17) A check of DEP records on 2/24/26 found that the operator had not submitted the Annual Production Report for 2025. Violations 78.121(A) and 78.121(B) are being cited for failure to submit annual production. A check of DEP records on 2/24/26 found that the operator has not submitted the Mechanical Integrity Assessment report for 2025. Violations 78.88(e), 78.88(b)1-4 and 78.88(d) are being cited for failure to submit integrity report. The operators posting is attached to the well tree. (Photograph #1) Using a Bascom Turner 611, calibrated on 2/13/26, no gas was detected around the well tree. (Photographs 6-16). The separators have surface corrosion but no signs of leaks, spills or equipment failure were noticed. No gas was detected around the equipment using the Bascom Turner 611. The production tank appears to be in sound condition, no signs of leaks or damage were found. The production tank is not attached to the production equipment. DEP recommend the tank be removed if it is no longer in use. Attached to the meter box is a former operator's posting. The sticker should be removed since it displays incorrect information as to the operator of the well. (Photograph #17)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/31/2024 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/31/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8212370
Permit API: 083-51666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/31/2024
Comments: Upon being made aware of a crude oil release near this conventional well, I contacted Pennhills and learned that a steel gathering line located along the eastern side of the road (downslope of this well) was found to be compromised on December 9, 2024 and actions were taken to repair the line and remediate impacted media at that time. Since that time, Pennhills has decommissioned and vac'd out all fluid from the compromised line and are currently using a different gathering line that parallels the western edge of the road to carry fluids from this well and others located beyond this location. Representatives of Pennhills stated that the bulk of the earth disturbance along the eastern edge of the road was conducted to locate the portion of the line that was leaking and that they constructed an underflow dam downslope of the road to contain residual product that continues to leach from the road bank due to the abundance of larger rocks and roots in the area. Upon my arrival for this inspection, I observed the disturbed area along the eastern edge of the road that accesses this well. There was no visual evidence of crude oil across this disturbance, which was temporarily stabilized with seed and mulch. Downslope of the road, an approximate 20'x30' area had soil exposed due to Pennhills' reported removal of oil soaked leaves from the area. Isolated pockets of crude oil remain throughout this area, which drains towards the underflow dam that is located approximately 100' east of the well [41.82619 -78.85691]. The underflow dam is functioning and appears to be regularly maintained, as there is currently only a minor sheen atop the standing water behind it.Crude oil was also observed on the surface at a recessed area approximately 30' east (41.82632 -78.85674 [downslope]) of the underflow dam that appears to have migrated subsurface from the vicinity of the underflow dam to this point.A second area of oil soaked leaves/soil was discovered approximately 30' south (41.82607 -78.85661) of the underflow dam in a currently dry channel.At this time, the constructed underflow dam and continued use of absorbent diapers/booms appear to be sufficient containment measures. It is highly suggested to regularly monitor the containment and evaluate downslope of the impacted area, particularly during and after rain and snowmelt events.The quantity of product released was unknown, but appears to be less than one barrel at this time. No watercourses have impacted by this incident at this time. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate if the current containment remains sufficient, if there was further migration of crude oil or evidence is presented that indicates the released quantity was greater than one barrel.

Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Upon inspection of the ground surrounding the corroded production tank, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#302235). This well is located approximately 1,444' from the complainants water well. The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. The well is equipped for production and is currently producing. The well is equipped with a required check valve. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation and are current. As part of the investigation 4 slam bar holes were placed into the ground in the cardinal directions approximately 6" to 1' from the well-head and approximately 3' deep to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II gas meter which was calibrated on 05/06/2024 was used to take the soil gas readings. A soil gas reading of 4% LEL on the North slam bar hole, 32% LEL on the East, 2% LEL on South, and 10% LEL on West was observed at the time of inspection. As a result of the soil gas readings around this well the following violations are being cited: Violation: 78.73(b) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to prevent gas, oil, brine, completion and servicing fluids, and any other fluids or materials from below the casing seat from entering fresh groundwater, and prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. Violation: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. Violation: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. At this time, the Department is requesting that the operator conduct an investigation to determine the source of methane around the well.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 973251
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/24/2022
Comments: On October 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. DEP spoke with Profrac Company Man Mike Reel and he said they were fracking the 1005H well at the time of inspection. The DEP observed multiple areas of staining adjacent to the containment for the fracking rig. The areas were screened for conductivity with a soil conductivity meter and two areas resulted in over range conductivity readings. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4.0 mS/cm. The first area is adjacent to the frack pumps off the east side of containment. This area of high conductivity is about 12' x 20'. The second area is adjacent to 1 frac tank and 2 gas buster tanks. This area of high conductivity is about 10'x10'. Soil sample 0651-139 was collected from the 10'x10' area. The volume of this spill is unknown because it is uncertain how much was spilled under the frack rig containment. The DEP pointed out the previously mentioned areas to Mr. Reel and he said he would have someone begin scraping up the areas immediately. DEP then placed a phone call to STL Resources Seth Rodriguez to inform him of the findings from the inspection. The DEP recommends assessing the area of elevated conductivity and updating DEP of the findings. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, the DEP recommends pursuing an Act 2 remediation. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in either of the stormwater vaults. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.2 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 3 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 31.7 uS/cm. Seep 4 was not screened due to the current condition of the seep screening area. This area is being driven through by ATVs checking on the freshwater waterline for the Sturgis South stimulation. The area is constantly being driven through to refuel the pumps on the waterline. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 24.7 uS/cm. The infiltration berms 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 11 along the access road are well vegetated and appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berms 1, 4, 6, 7, and 9 along the access road are vegetated but, the areas that are holding water have little vegetation and do not appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 1 off the northwest corner of the pad appears to be holding water and not functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 2 off the northwest corner of the pad and the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the pad are lacking vegetation in the infiltration area. The DEP recommends working on the infiltration berms that are not functioning correctly and reseeding the infiltration berms that are lacking vegetation to prevent an erosion event. The areas of staining along with the elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment on the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MCCOOL JOHN E
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8278639
Permit API: 123-47075
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Cherry Grove Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2026
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to the observation of production fluid exiting the secondary containment of the Lot 740 tank battery. Conventional well Lot 740 15 (API # 123-47075) is nearest the tank battery. The conventional well appears to be plumbed for production. An old sign displaying the API number, well name, and the wrong operator contact information is posted on a tree near the location. The sign should be updated with the current operator's name and contact information. The tank battery at the site has 2 steel tanks and a separator situated within an earthen secondary containment. The secondary containment was approximately 60ft x 20ft. Evidence of staining, dead vegetation, numerous deer tracks, and conductivity readings over range (greater than 20,000 mS/cm maximum that field meter can measure) were present in standing water throughout the entire secondary containment. This would indicate a large volume of production fluid filled the entire containment at one time (see photo 1). At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Inspection Date: 3/02/2021
Comments: This inspection report is written to document an incident response inspection conducted in response of a lube oil spill on the well site. Hilcorp Energy contacted the Department via telephone at approximately 9:50 AM on 3/2/21 to report a spill of lube oil close to the compressor on this McCullough well site. The volume lost was 175 gallons. I arrived on site at approximately 1:20 PM on 3/2/21. It appeared that somehow a leak developed from the elevated storage tank for the lube oil. This tank was located near the compressor unit for this well site. Most of the lube oil was cleaned up and material was placed in two drums on location. Very little oil was able to be seen on the ground surface, just staining. There were several 4" booms on the ground surface mostly surrounding the extent of the spill. The impacted area is roughly 15' x 25'. I called Brett Bunker and verified the details about the spill. He said a broken site tube on the tank was the cause of the spill. He said they will be back out tomorrow to start digging up the contaminated material (gravel and dirt). Laterally, the spill was contained. Vertically, Brett felt the oil would not travel much farther overnight. It was mentioned that because of the amount spilled, the clean-up would fall under the requirements of Chapter 78a.66 of the regulations. The contractor, S.E.T. Contracting from Lowellville Ohio, arrived while I was there and started unloading equipment for the clean-up.

Comments: On 06/22/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Pizzi 4 well following a Department issued Spill Order sent to the operator on 05/11/2023 via email.It is recommended to ensure that well transfer paperwork is obtained by the Department. The following was observed during inspection:Impacted substrate appeared to not have been remediated and straw applied to area (Photos 1-8); impacted material will need to be removed from site and a waste manifest provided to the Department. Elevated conductivity was observed (Photos 2-6). Fluid level in tank appeared to be lower (Photo 8).Areas of fluid that was recommended to be addressed in IR 3569077 (Photos 9, 10). Pipe observed in vegetation, which appeared to be the pipe referenced in IR 356907 associated with the fluid (Photos 11, 12).Gravel pile observed onsite (Photo 13).Regarding the access road and earth disturbance, it appears a culvert has been constructed to divert water from the excavated channel along the site access road, documented in IR 3537433 (Photos 14, 15).The culvert appears to discharge off the hillside into the woods with no riprap at the discharge point observed (Photos 16, 17). It appears that this area has potential for accelerated erosion and transport of sediment down slope (Photos 14-19).Stabilization has not been applied to disturbed area and minimal vegetation observed (Photos 14, 15, 18, 19). A permit for culvert installation has not been obtained from the Department. Violations of 102.4(b)4, 102.4(b)1, 102.22(b)1, and 102.22(a) are being issued for failure to implement the use of Best Management Practices (BMPs) including temporary stabilization, permanent stabilization, and perimeter control for the protection from accelerated erosion and sedimentation.Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further inspection.

Due to the CHK's quick response and self-reporting of the incident, the result of this inspection is Violations Immediately Corrected.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 369107 dated 12/30/2022.A complaint was emailed to the Department regarding a tank overflow of produced fluid from the 100bbl steel storage tank onsite.Upon arriving at the site, produced fluid was observed on the side of the tank, tank steps, and pooled within the earthen dike. Oil product was also observed to be on the side of the 50bbl poly tank and around the thief hatch of the tank. It appears that the 100bbl steel tank had overflowed and released approximately 15-20 gallons of produced fluid to the ground within the earthen dike. It appears that an unknown amount of fluid (oil) was scrapped up and put into the 50bbl poly tank. The released fluids were contained to the earthen dike.The operator was contacted via phone while still onsite. The operator was unaware of the extent of the release. Since the release was being contained to the earthen dike, the operator stated that a cleanup crew would be onsite first thing in the morning to cleanup the release.1/4/2022 (11:00am)I stopped at the site and visual cleanup operations were nearly complete. The impacted area within the dike was scrapped up with an excavator and placed into a dump truck. Fresh clean gravel was onsite to reclaim the inside of the earthen dike. The impacted material will be hauled to their shop for future disposal.A follow-up inspection will be conducted by the Department once cleanup is completed.Violations are cited.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Tilden Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-04
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 851519
Permit API: 117-20476
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Elk Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-04
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 6/4/2019 @0930 hours. The weather was 62 degrees and sunny. Jennifer Compton, Rockdale/Tilden Marcellus, and Korey Starkey, DEP Env Trainee, was present onsite for the inspection. On 6/3/2019 at 23:20,a nitrogen pop-off unit failed allowing stimulation fluid to spray out onto containment and the grassy area surrounding the pad. Tilden deployed vac trucks to collect and return the fluid to the onsite tanks. As of today's inspection, fluid with a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm was observed pooling on the eastern and southeastern edges of the pad. A skid steer was being used to scrape up vegetation and soils, on the eastern fill slope, with an elevated field measured conductivity. Damp areas with soil exhibiting a field measured conductivity of >4.0mS/cm were observed off the southeastern corner of the pad and underneath the rig mats in the sand storage area. There is no containment under the sand storage area. A representative from Tilden's environmental contractor, C.E.C., arrived onsite and began delineating the extent of the impacted soils. Approximately 2 acres of vegetation appeared to have salt crystallization, from evaporating stimulation fluid, deposited on it. This impacted vegetation was observed to tree line east southeast of the well pad. Tilden Marcellus's spill response plan involved brush-hogging and weed whacking all impacted vegetation. This vegetation would be bagged and disposed of in an appropriate container. Impacted pad material and soils would also be removed and placed in onsite waste containers. A lined trench and sumps would be installed, in the east and southeast fill slopes, to intercept any stormwater runoff that commingled with a regulated substance from the site (thereby becoming a regulated substance). Fluid with a field measured conductivity of 13.64mS/cm was observed pooling, outside of containment, along the interior edge of the sand storage area. Sample 4427-187 was collected from this fluid. Fluid with a field measured conductivity was observed in numerous areas inside the secondary containment. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a56(a) We departed the site at 1230 hours.
